text: Friends, let me remind you of the good news I brought you, the one you took in and still stand on.
It is saving you too, as long as you hold to what I told you — otherwise your belief was for nothing.
The first thing I handed on to you, because it was handed to me: Christ died for our sins, as the writings foretold.
He was laid in a grave and, on the third day, raised up, again just as the writings foretold.
He showed himself to Cephas first, and afterward to the group of the Twelve.
Then more than five hundred of his followers saw him together; most are still alive, though a few have died.
After that he appeared to James, and then to all the apostles.
Last of all he appeared to me too, like someone born at the wrong time.
I'm the least of the apostles, hardly fit to bear the name, since I once hounded God's church.
But by God's gift I am what I am, and that gift was not wasted; I worked harder than any of them — really his gift at work in me.
So whether it was me or them, this is what we announce and what you came to believe.
If the message is that Christ was raised, how can some of you say there is no rising of the dead?
If there is no rising of the dead, then Christ was not raised either.
And if Christ was not raised, our message is empty, and so is your faith.
We would even be caught lying about God, claiming he raised Christ when he did not, if the dead are never raised.
For if the dead are not raised, neither was Christ.
And if Christ was not raised, your faith is futile and you are still stuck in your sins.
Then those who died trusting Christ are simply lost.
If our hope in Christ reaches only to this life, we are the most pitiable people there are.
But in fact Christ has been raised, the first portion of the harvest of those who have died.
Death came through a man, and so the rising of the dead comes through a man.
As everyone dies through Adam, so everyone will be brought to life through Christ.
Each in turn: Christ first, then those who belong to him when he returns.
Then comes the end, when he hands the kingdom to God the Father after putting down every rule, authority and power.
He must reign until all his enemies are under his feet.
The last enemy to be destroyed is death.
Scripture says everything is put under his feet — obviously the one who does the putting is not included.
When everything is placed under the Son, the Son will place himself under God, so that God is all in all.
Otherwise, what are people doing when they are baptized for the dead? If the dead never rise, why do it?
And why do we put ourselves in danger every hour?
I face death daily — I swear it by my pride in you.
If the dead don't rise, what did I gain fighting wild beasts at Ephesus? We might as well eat and drink, for tomorrow we die.
Don't be fooled: bad company corrupts good habits.
Wake up and live rightly; some of you don't know God, and I say it to shame you.
Someone will ask, how are the dead raised? What kind of body do they come with?
Foolish question! What you plant doesn't come alive unless it first dies.
And what you plant is not the plant it will become, just a bare seed of wheat or something else.
God gives it the body he chose, each kind of seed its own.
Not all flesh is the same: people, animals, birds and fish each differ.
There are heavenly bodies and earthly bodies, each with its own splendor.
The sun has one glory, the moon another, the stars another, and star differs from star.
So it is with the rising of the dead: what is sown is perishable; what is raised is imperishable.
Sown in dishonor, raised in glory; sown in weakness, raised in power.
Sown a natural body, raised a spiritual body. If there is a natural body, there is a spiritual one too.
So it is written: the first man Adam became a living being; the last Adam became a life-giving spirit.
The spiritual did not come first, but the natural, and then the spiritual.
The first man came from the earth's dust; the second man comes from heaven.
Those made of dust are like the man of dust; those who are heavenly are like the heavenly man.
Just as we have borne the likeness of the man of dust, we will bear the likeness of the man from heaven.
This I tell you, friends: flesh and blood cannot inherit God's kingdom, and the perishable cannot inherit the imperishable.
Listen, here is a secret: we won't all die, but we will all be changed.
In an instant, in the blink of an eye, at the last trumpet — the trumpet will sound, the dead will be raised imperishable, and we will be changed.
This perishable body must put on the imperishable, and this mortal body must put on immortality.
When the perishable puts on the imperishable and the mortal puts on immortality, the saying will come true: death is swallowed up in victory.
Death, where is your victory? Death, where is your sting?
Death's sting is sin, and sin's strength is the law.
But thanks be to God, who gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ!
So, my dear friends, stand firm and unshakable, always giving yourselves fully to the Lord's work, knowing your labor in him is never wasted.
